fatal_errors: The material is misidentified as an FCC/σ-phase alloy rather than the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 L12/B2 lamellar eutectic HEA.

The proposed approximately 300 °C chloride-electrolyte exposure is incompatible with the target 25–100 °C deionized-water tests and is underspecified because liquid water at 300 °C requires a pressurized apparatus.
The matched DS2205 comparator and the rapid 1100 °C heating/quenching treatment are omitted.

The proposed phase-boundary galvanic-corrosion mechanism is not established for the target alloy; the target mechanism centers on temperature-dependent competition among depassivation, repassivation, and tribo-layer stability.
The prediction misses the observed nonmonotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and maximum degradation at 100 °C.
The cited evidence concerns different Mo-bearing laser-clad alloys and cannot establish the claimed mechanism in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 under the target conditions.
explanation: The response addresses the general concept of accelerated coupled wear and corrosion and correctly recognizes that oxide-film rupture can expose fresh metal and alter wear. That limited feature overlaps with the high-temperature tribo-layer disruption observed at 100 °C. Otherwise, it reconstructs a different material system, environment, temperature, microstructure, comparator, and dominant mechanism. Its isolated wear-only and corrosion-only controls could test whether a synergy exists, but they do not distinguish the target explanation from alternatives such as thermally activated repassivation, compacted tribo-layer formation, or third-body abrasion. The proposed interfacial-chemistry modification is also confounded because heat treatment or microalloying may change hardness, phase fraction, and wear resistance independently of oxidation homogeneity. Evidence E1–E3 gives analogical support for oxide rupture and galvanic effects in Mo- and σ-containing HEA coatings, not direct support for the target L12/B2 alloy. A stronger reconstruction would compare identically conditioned AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and DS2205 in deionized water at 25, 50, and 100 °C, predicting minimum wear near 50 °C, patchy tribo-layer rupture at 100 °C, and substantially lower and more stable HEA degradation.
